body.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the three signed measures
\[
 \gamma_v^\pm=\lambda_v^\pm-3p_0^\dagger,
 \qquad \gamma_d^\pm=\lambda_d^\pm-2p_0^\dagger,
 \qquad \gamma_0=\delta_{111}-\delta_{000}
\]
have total mass zero and respective centered marginal moments \(\pm v\), \(\pm d^\dagger\), and \(\mathbf1\).  Their target first moments are \(\pm1\), \(0\), and \(0\), and their target second moments are \(5/8\), \(3/16\), and \(0\).  The law in \(\mathrm{def:explicit\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}airy\text{-}tube}\) is therefore a probability distribution whenever \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1\), and it satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E[b_t\mid x,h,\zeta]
 =\alpha_n(xv+hd^\dagger+\zeta\mathbf1),
 \quad
 \mathbb E[\theta_t\mid x,h,\zeta]=\alpha_nx,
 \quad
 \mathbb E[\theta_t^2\mid x,h,\zeta]
 =\alpha_n\left\{\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
For the three two-arm faces \(F=\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}\), respectively, the paths
\[
 (h_F(x),\zeta_F(x))
 =\left(\frac43x,-\frac12x\right),
 \quad
 (-4x,-\tfrac12x),
 \quad
 (0,\tfrac12x)
 \tag{2}
\]
have target derivative one and zero marginal derivative on every arm in \(F\).  Each single-arm face is contained in one of these faces.  The corresponding positive and negative signed response-type directions have target-second-moment costs \(7/8\), \(11/8\), and \(5/8\).  For every \(|x|\leq1\), all six paths give probability laws once \(\alpha_n\leq1/10\); hence the face-guard width is fixed, rather than vanishing with \(n\).
body.proof_tex:
The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
 \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm=3,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm b_t=\pm v,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm\theta_t=\pm1,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm\theta_t^2=\frac58,
 \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm=2,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm b_t=\pm d^\dagger,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm\theta_t=0,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm\theta_t^2=\frac3{16}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Both atoms of \(p_0^\dagger\) have \(\theta_t=0\), while
\(\sum_tp_{0,t}^\dagger b_t=0\).  Also
\[
 \sum_t(\delta_{111}-\delta_{000})(t)b_t
 =b_{111}-b_{000}=\mathbf1,
 \qquad
 \theta_{111}=\theta_{000}=0,
 \tag{5}
\]
where the last equality uses \(\sum_ac_a^\dagger=0\).  Subtracting the indicated multiples of \(p_0^\dagger\) in (3)--(5) proves every mass, marginal, target-first-moment, and target-second-moment assertion about \(\gamma_v^\pm,\gamma_d^\pm,\gamma_0\).  Substitution in the construction then proves (1).

It remains to check positivity and the faces.  Away from the types \(000\) and \(111\), the perturbation is a sum of nonnegative multiples of the displayed \(\lambda\)'s.  At either central type its negative part is bounded by
\[
 \alpha_n\left(\frac32|x|+|h|+|\zeta|\right)
 \leq\frac12
\]
under \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1\).  Since the central mass is \(1/2\), all eight coordinates are nonnegative; the zero-total-mass identities make their sum one.  This proves exact positivity.

For a pair \(F\), write
\(z_F(x)=xv+h_F(x)d^\dagger+\zeta_F(x)\mathbf1\).  Direct substitution of
\[
 v=(1/2,-1/2,-1/2),
 \qquad d^\dagger=(0,3/4,-1/4)
\]
gives
\[
 z_{\{1,2\}}(x)=(0,0,-4x/3),
 \quad
 z_{\{1,3\}}(x)=(0,-4x,0),
 \quad
 z_{\{2,3\}}(x)=(x,0,0).
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus the observed marginal slopes on the indicated face are zero.  Moreover
\((c^\dagger)^\top z_F(x)=x\), either from (6) or from
\((c^\dagger)^\top v=1\),
\((c^\dagger)^\top d^\dagger=0\), and
\((c^\dagger)^\top\mathbf1=0\).  Hence every path has target derivative one.  Combining the second moments in (3)--(5), its cost per unit \(|x|\) is
\[
 \frac58+\frac43\frac3{16}=\frac78,
 \qquad
 \frac58+4\frac3{16}=\frac{11}{8},
 \qquad
 \frac58,
 \tag{7}
\]
respectively.  Finally, direct inspection of the two central coordinates of each of the six signed directions shows that their largest negative coefficient in absolute value is at most five; all noncentral coefficients are nonnegative.  Therefore \(p_0^\dagger+\alpha_n|x|\Gamma_F^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}\) is nonnegative for \(|x|\leq1\) whenever \(5\alpha_n\leq1/2\).  This is \(\alpha_n\leq1/10\), and proves the fixed-width assertion.
